paper.title_en: Traversable wormholes in Hernquist dark matter halos: Photon spheres, quasinormal modes, and echo-like signatures
paper.abstract_en: We investigate a traversable Morris–Thorne wormhole supported by a Hernquist dark-matter halo, in which the Hernquist central density controls both the optical appearance and the scalar-wave scattering properties of the geometry. We show that two critical densities govern the photon-sphere structure and use them to compute the shadow radius and strong-deflection lensing coefficients. We further show that the central density drives a topological transition in the scalar effective potential, from a single throat-centered barrier to a symmetric double-barrier configuration. In the single-barrier regime, third-order WKB and direct time-domain evolution agree at the percent level, confirming linear mode stability with longer-lived, lower-frequency ringdown as central density increases. In the double-barrier regime, time-domain evolution reveals delayed, echo-like modulations whose separation scales with the cavity width, while real-frequency scattering calculations reveal narrow, multipole-dependent graybody resonances with near-unit transmission at selected frequencies. These results provide a unified optical and wave-scattering characterization of a two-ended, dark-matter-supported wormhole.
